name: Caribbean Tamarind balls
assumptions: Yield estimated at 20 marble-sized balls based on 454g tamarind pulp (typical ~20-25g per ball after mixing); conservative classification as exact count not specified

Total time estimated at 30 minutes: ~10 min mashing/mixing, ~15 min rolling balls and coating in sugar, ~5 min for optional setting prep; no cooking or extended wait included as 'immediate' consumption is allowed
All sugar (1.5 cups total) is used per provided ingredient data (1 cup mashed + 0.5 cup coating); no other ingredients or compounds present
Tamarind pulp treated as pure fruit pulp with no additives, per conservative screening and Jamaican dessert context
No gluten sources (barley/rye/wheat/oats) present; recipe is inherently plant-based with no animal products
instructions:
Add tamarind pulp and 1 cup granulated sugar to a bowl and mash together with a spoon or fork. Take small amounts of the tamarind and sugar mix and shape them into small balls by rolling them in your hands. Make them the size of a marble or slightly bigger, as you like.
Add the remaining sugar to a flat surface, like a plate or a sheet pan. Roll the tamarind balls in granulated sugar until they're well-coated.
You can eat the tamarind balls immediately, or you can let them set for a few hours or overnight. Allowing them to set will give them a firmer texture and more crystallized sugar coating. Enjoy.

ingredients.name: Tamarind Pulp
ingredients.assumptions: 16 oz tamarind pulp estimated at 454g; using typical values for tamarind pulp with seeds removed as implied by 'pulp' in a candy recipe; raw edible portion.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.assumptions: 1.5 cups granulated sugar estimated at 300g (standard 200g per cup); all sugar is used in the recipe (1 cup mashed in + 0.5 cup for coating).
